content.text: To build an argument, state your conclusion, gather premises that support it, check that it follows, and answer the strongest objection.

content.definition: Premises that work together. Take one away and the support fails.
Premises that each support the conclusion on their own.

examples.title: Convergent
examples.note: Each premise gives its own reason. Losing one leaves the others.

question.prompt: In a linked argument, what happens if one premise is removed?
options: The rest no longer support the conclusion
question.hint: Linked premises work together, like links in a chain.
question.explanation: Linked premises support the conclusion only together. Take one away and the support fails.
